lines:
Responsibilities: Is the single-flight durable orchestration policy for managed-local enrollment preparation, activation, rollback, relaunch, and result production. The enrollment transaction is fixed and nonactivating: while no activation is active it validates ManagedLocalEnrollmentRequestV1, obtains an EnrollmentPlanV1, materializes and verifies the helper-controlled root, and returns EnrollmentPreparedV1 so the user can later restart through the stable launcher. It consumes only an admitted BootstrapCommandV1, drives journaled preflight, quiescence, selector switch, candidate launch/watchdog and focused-verification handoff, commits Verified only after all proofs pass, or deterministically stops the candidate, restores/reverifies the previous slot, relaunches it, and emits the protected BootstrapResultV1 for the next core generation.

Owned state/files: Owns an ephemeral ActivationAggregateV1 rebuilt from the journal: ActivationId, accepted RepairActivationBatonV1 hash, ManagedLocalBuildProfileV1 version, installation ID, enrollment digest, capability-generation digest, BootstrapPhaseV1, verified candidate and previous slots, ActivationPlanV1, effect-intent IDs, current, candidate and rollback ProcessGenerationV1 values, bounded retry and deadline budgets, selector and process observations, verification-plan and CapabilityOutcomeV1 hashes, rollback reason, next-core identity, ManualRecoveryNoticeV1, and receipt draft. During onboarding it owns a separate ephemeral EnrollmentAggregateV1 with EnrollmentId, request and provenance hashes, EnrollmentPlanV1, publication intents, and EnrollmentPreparedV1 draft. The activation journal owns all durable files and the slot/profile/watchdog modules own their mechanics.

Ports/DTOs: ActivationControlPortV1 accepts PrepareManagedLocalEnrollment, StartAdmittedActivation, and RecoverActivation. It calls ActivationJournalPortV1, BuildSlotVerifyPortV1, PlatformActivationPortV1, and ApplicationLaunchWatchdogPortV1. BootstrapResultReadPortV1 makes the immutable BootstrapResultV1 available to the exact candidate core after success or freshly relaunched previous core after rollback. BootstrapResultV1 records ActivatedVerified, RolledBack, Unsupported, AbortedBeforeSwitch, or ManualRecoveryRequired with slot/generation identities, ordered proof hashes, verification disposition, reason, journal head, helper/profile versions, and SameUserHashAndOwnership integrity descriptor.

Phase and generation invariants: Enrollment may start only from a bounded LocalSourceBuild request while no activation or other enrollment is active; it never quiesces the current build, accepts arbitrary paths, or marks the prepared slot activated. The core Repair Orchestrator may hand off activation only after durable explicit Activate and restart approval, complete disclosure hash, ManagementCheckpointRefV1, candidate/previous hashes, and canonical commit acknowledgement. The coordinator does not infer that gate. It maintains exactly one phase writer. Current authority ends before candidate authority can begin; the candidate remains verification-only until Verified is durable. A failed or missing identity/health/CapabilityOutcomeV1, expired deadline, helper crash in a destructive phase, or candidate exit triggers rollback. Rollback order is fixed: journal intent, terminate complete candidate tree, restore and reverify previous selector/slot, launch a fresh rollback ProcessGenerationV1, authenticate its handshake, then store RolledBack. No automatic second repair or helper self-update is permitted.

Atomic and crash behavior: Every external effect has durable intent, exact execution parameters, observed result, and a phase transition. Recovery compares the journal with opened slot, selector, and process-tree identities and resumes only a proven idempotent step. Before an activation selector change a failure leaves the current build and records AbortedBeforeSwitch or Unsupported. Enrollment uses a new temporary managed root and atomic publication; failure leaves the original source build running and any incomplete root unreachable. After selector change uncertainty is rollback-biased. A durable passing verification result may be finalized after crash only when its exact generation, plan, deadline, selector, and CapabilityOutcomeV1 hash are present; otherwise rollback. Rollback retries are bounded per exact idempotent operation. Corrupt previous slot, failed restoration or relaunch, forward-only data migration, disk exhaustion, or ownership and permission loss after switching produces ManualRecoveryRequired and never chooses an arbitrary build. If no core can launch, the coordinator journals ManualRecoveryNoticeV1 for the stable launcher; a later successful core imports the same receipt into Management Chat.

Security, integrity, and privilege semantics: The coordinator can invoke only the fixed typed ports and exact baton resources. It never accepts generic commands/paths, loads extensions, stores secrets, or inherits workflow authority. BootstrapResultV1 is sealed only after journal durability and records the profile's honest SameUserHashAndOwnership integrity strength. The next core must authenticate with the expected ProcessGenerationV1 to read it. Receipt delivery is not a semantic commit: the newly launched core routes activation/rollback evidence through its Repair Orchestrator and sole Canonical Event Committer before Recovery resumes the same Management Chat.

Cross-platform degradation: Orchestration branches only on typed PlatformCapabilityReportV1 and observations, never OS-name heuristics. Packaged or unknown origin, enrollment mismatch, elevation requirement, package ownership, lost atomicity, helper or launcher survival failure, tree-cleanup failure, unavailable verification-only mode, incompatible data, or missing previous-slot preservation returns Unsupported before quiescence. Only a guarantee lost after switching can enter rollback or ManualRecoveryRequired. Platform-specific adapters may offer different strength, which is recorded in BootstrapResultV1 rather than normalized into a false universal guarantee.

NFRs: State transitions are deterministic, single-writer, bounded, and fully reason-coded; retry and deadline budgets are conservative and configuration-versioned in the baton; recovery and terminal receipt creation are idempotent; result availability survives IPC loss and reboot; observability includes phase duration, rollback trigger, retry exhaustion, result integrity strength, and manual-recovery reason without secret or Chat payload logging.

Non-responsibilities: Does not diagnose, edit, compile, benchmark, download, install arbitrary packages or accept arbitrary enrollment paths, run focused verification or general tools, approve the repair, grant workflow authority, manage secrets, write the error-repair ledger, commit or resume Chat history itself, repair forward-migrated application data, depend on UI/worker/capability-host/portable-store, start another repair, or update the helper during the same activation.

data.name: Activation, Rollback & Result Coordinator
data.technology: Rust single-flight durable activation state machine over typed bootstrap ports
